newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta economy expected to grow four pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Malta economy expected to grow four pct in 1997.

text.p: Malta's economy is expected to grow by four percent in real terms in 1997, the same as in 1996, according to Central Bank governor Francis Vassallo.

Writing in the bank's annual report for 1996, Vassallo said the economy appeared to be at a turning point. Domestic demand was slowing but foreign demand was expected to grow in 1997 as the economies of Malta's trading partners, mainly Europe, picked up.
Tourism was also expected to start recovering after declining in the past two years, he said in the bank's report released late on Monday.

"The moderate rise of GDP growth is expected to be accompanied by a slight rise in unemployment and a relatively stable rate of inflation within the range of 2.5 percent to three percent," Vassallo said.

The report says retail price inflation reached 2.5 percent in 1996. GDP rose by 7.4 percent in nominal terms and 4.2 percent in real terms. This was roughly comparable to growth in 1993 and 1994 but lower than in 1995 when figures were distorted as Value Added Tax revealed a substantial chunk of the black economy.
Unemployment in 1996 rose to 3.7 percent from 3.4 percent a year earlier.
Nominal private consumption expenditure rose by 11 percent in 1996 but the growth of household disposable income slowed to eight percent due to a slowdown in the growth of incomes.

The household savings ratio fell to eight percent in 1996 from 10 percent in 1995 and 17 percent in 1994. The bank said the generally buoyant economy and inflated real estate prices could have been behind this development.
